stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Brokers Sale of 280-Unit Oswego Apartment Property
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has brokered the sale of Springs at Oswego, a 280-unit apartment community in Oswego, Illinois, one of Chicago’s fastest-growing western suburbs.Cushman & Wakefield’s Brad Smith and Jack Maloney represented the seller, Continental Properties, a national developer and operator of multifamily, retail and hospitality properties. The buyer was Oak Brook, Illinois-based JVM Realty.Located at 801 Fifth St., and originally developed in 2019, Springs at Oswego comprises 14 two-story residential buildings situated on 27.5 acres. The townhome-style community offers studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom floorplans ranging from 623 to 1,430 square feet. “Springs at Oswego is a best-in-class suburban community that generated exceptional investor interest, evidenced by more than 20 qualified offers,” said Brad Smith, Managing Director at Cushman & Wakefield. “The property’s strong demographics, on-site amenities, distinctive design and location within one of the Chicago region’s fastest-growing corridors position it to benefit from sustained renter demand and long-term growth.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: Continental Properties sold 280-unit Springs at Oswego (2019) to JVM Realty; 20+ offers received.
Oswego, Illinois is one of Chicago's fastest-growing western suburbs with strong demographics.
Townhome-style product (623–1,430 sq ft) on 27.5 acres signals suburban renter demand strength.
stories.summary: Continental Properties sold Springs at Oswego, a 280-unit townhome-style community completed in 2019, to JVM Realty in a competitive sale attracting 20+ qualified offers. The property is located in Oswego, Illinois, a rapidly growing western Chicago suburb, and comprises 14 two-story buildings on 27.5 acres with studio to three-bedroom units. Strong investor interest and broker commentary on sustained renter demand underscore the submarket's appeal.
stories.impact: Oswego's competitive bidding and rapid lease-up signal robust demand in western Chicago exurbs. For developers, this validates suburban townhome product and timing to acquire/entitle near I-88 or in similar commuter corridors before land costs escalate further; suburban densification ahead of population inflow to outer ring creates window.

stories.title: Castle Lanterra Completes Sale of 224-Unit Residential Property in Suffolk
stories.excerpt: Castle Lanterra announced the sale of Meridian Obici, a 224-unit multifamily community located in Suffolk, Virginia, within the Hampton Roads metropolitan area.Completed in 2016, Meridian Obici is a highly amenitized multifamily community featuring a resort-style saltwater swimming pool, fitness and business centers, resident entertainment spaces, outdoor kitchens, detached garages, storage units, and a dog park. The property is situated along Suffolk’s North Main Street corridor, providing residents with convenient access to retail, dining, and essential services.CL acquired Meridian Obici in October 2018 for approximately $32 million, or $143,000 per unit, which allowed the company to own a recently constructed, stabilized asset at an attractive basis within one of Virginia’s fastest-growing regional economies. The property provides connectivity to major employment hubs throughout Newport News, Norfolk, Virginia Beach, and the surrounding metropolitan area. Suffolk is within Hampton Roads metro, connecting to Newport News, Norfolk, Virginia Beach employment.

stories.summary: Castle Lanterra sold Meridian Obici, a 224-unit amenitized multifamily community in Suffolk, Virginia, which it acquired in October 2018 for approximately $32 million ($143,000 per unit). The property, completed in 2016, is situated in the Hampton Roads metro and provides connectivity to major employment hubs. The sale demonstrates the company's value-add strategy and exit after stabilization.
stories.impact: Hampton Roads (Norfolk/Virginia Beach/Newport News corridor) remains underutilized by multifamily developers relative to military/federal employment base and population. Suffolk's location on North Main Street and connectivity to three major cities signal rising demand; developers should monitor naval base expansions and federal workforce trends that could unlock mid-market rent growth before coastal VA becomes saturated.

stories.title: HITT Contracting Stays a Step Ahead
stories.excerpt: A nationwide contractor with 16 offices across the U.S., HITT Contracting has been performing work in California for more than 20 years and has offices in Los Angeles, Santa Clara, and San Francisco. The nature of its projects and the demands of building them have certainly evolved over time, but the company considers its involvement from the early stages of design to be a competitive advantage. Connect CRE spoke with Trevor Coffey, Executive Vice President for the West Coast and Southwest regions, about the ways in which the company maintains its edge in the California marketplace.  We’ve seen California grow more prominent in the aerospace, hard-tech and advanced manufacturing ecosystem. What are the drivers of this growth for California, especially Southern California, and what are the implications for the manufacturers’ real estate and facility requirements?  Existing talent and a strong military presence are a big part of it, and on top of that, there’s the increased capital investment. Defense tech, aerospace and hard tech have gained a lot of attention just in the past year and a half. At midyear 2026, funding had already surpassed the more than $9 billion raised in 2025. Trevor Coffey In Southern California specifically, there’s traditionally been a strong culture of startups and these types of companies planting a flag here. The South Bay of Los Angeles, including Hawthorne, El Segundo, Torrance, and Long Beach, has been a central hub, and cities like El Segundo add real value with a business-friendly tax environment and streamlined permitting. One great example is Anduril’s upcoming large development in Long Beach, in addition to their Costa Mesa campus in Orange County. Much of the growth in the South Bay, though, has been driven by the ecosystems surrounding companies like SpaceX, Northrop Grumman, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Lab and others. bullets: HITT Contracting reports aerospace/hard-tech/defense funding in SoCal exceeded $9B by mid-2026; 2025 full-year was >$9B.
South Bay (Hawthorne, El Segundo, Torrance, Long Beach) remains hub; Anduril expanding in Long Beach and Costa Mesa.

stories.summary: HITT Contracting highlights Southern California's growing prominence in aerospace, hard-tech, and advanced manufacturing, with funding exceeding $9 billion by mid-2026 versus $9 billion for all of 2025. The South Bay—including Hawthorne, El Segundo, Torrance, and Long Beach—remains the central hub, with companies like Anduril expanding campuses. Cities like El Segundo offer business-friendly tax environments and streamlined permitting that attract talent and capital.
stories.impact: Aerospace/defense tech boom in SoCal (especially South Bay and Orange County) will drive sustained job creation and in-migration of engineers and technical talent, increasing renter demand in coastal and near-coastal submarkets. Developers should prioritize workforce housing near El Segundo, Long Beach, and Torrance; labor-intensive manufacturing often requires 24/7 operations, favoring proximate multifamily. Monitor Anduril and peer hiring/leasing announcements for demand signals 12–18 months ahead of occupancy.

stories.title: EYA, Armed Forces Mutual Secure Entitlement for MF Project at Historic Reston Site
stories.excerpt: EYA and Armed Forces Mutual have secured entitlement for the redevelopment of Armed Forces Mutual’s Reston Campus at 1850 Old Reston Avenue into a 57-townhome community centered around the historic Bowman House. The milestone marks a significant step toward transforming the underutilized office campus into a residential neighborhood. Located adjacent to the W&OD Trail and just a five-minute walk from Reston Town Center, the community will feature 57 fee-simple townhomes, including seven affordable dwelling units. The homes will offer a range of floor plans with rooftop terraces while thoughtfully integrating the site’s historic assets, including the Bowman House and its iconic gazebo. The Bowman House will be preserved through adaptive reuse and positioned for conversion into a single-family residence, with office use retained as an alternative future option. Groundbreaking is anticipated in spring 2027, with sales expected to begin in fall 2027. bullets: EYA and Armed Forces Mutual secure entitlement for 57-townhome redevelopment at 1850 Old Reston Avenue, Reston VA.

Adjacent to W&OD Trail, 5-minute walk to Reston Town Center; office conversion signals transit-oriented demand shift.
stories.summary: EYA and Armed Forces Mutual have secured entitlement for redeveloping Armed Forces Mutual's underutilized Reston office campus into a 57-townhome fee-simple community, including seven affordable dwelling units. Groundbreaking is anticipated in spring 2027, with sales beginning in fall 2027. The site's historic Bowman House will be adaptively reused, and the location offers walkability to Reston Town Center and proximity to the W&OD Trail.
stories.impact: Reston's office-to-residential conversion (declining corporate real estate demand) coupled with strong for-sale townhome product validates Northern Virginia's shift toward live-work-play density. Developers should scout similar underutilized office parks along Metro corridors and rail/trail access in Loudoun and Fairfax counties; entitled, transit-adjacent parcels command premium financing and faster absorption, particularly for for-sale communities.

stories.title: Timberlane Partners Acquires 91-Unit Issaquah Apartments for $37M
stories.excerpt: Seattle-based real estate investment firm Timberlane Partners has acquired the Vista Ridge, a 91-unit apartment complex in Issaquah, for $37 million. The 91-unit apartment complex at 201 Mountain Park Blvd. SW sold in a deal, with the sale price coming out to around $406,600 per unit, reported the Puget Sound Business Journal. The seller was Vancouver, British Columbia-based Belkorp Holdings. Vista Ridge offers two- and three-bedroom apartments and is located near historic downtown Issaquah and Gilman Village. The property benefits from proximity to the trails, local shopping, dining, and outdoor destination and the complex provides convenient access to I-90 and SR 900. The 107,077-square-foot Vista Ridge was built in 1992. The eight-building, garden-style complex sits on 7 acres and includes two- and three-bedroom apartments averaging 1,106 square feet. Timberlane acquired Vista Ridge through its Timberlane Acquisition Fund II. It is the third acquisition for the fund, following the purchases of Wonderland Creek Townhomes in Colorado and the Jackson Apartments in Seattle. stories.summary: Seattle-based Timberlane Partners acquired Vista Ridge, a 91-unit garden-style apartment complex in Issaquah, Washington, for $37 million ($406,600 per unit). The 1992-built property sits on 7 acres near downtown Issaquah and I-90. This is the third acquisition for Timberlane Acquisition Fund II, following purchases in Colorado and Seattle, signaling a focus on the Pacific Northwest.
stories.impact: Issaquah, a Puget Sound submarket with proximity to I-90 and suburban employment (tech campus migration from Seattle), supports acquisition multiples at $407k/unit for stabilized garden product—indicating investor confidence in Seattle metro rental demand despite tech sector volatility. Developers should monitor tech headcount trends and potential satellite office openings in Issaquah; supply-constrained outer ring may support new construction if zoning allows density near transit corridors.

stories.title: Ares Buys Two Fully Leased Miami Warehouses for $109M
stories.excerpt: Ares Management has acquired two fully leased warehouses in Miami-Dade County from BGRE for a combined $108.7 million, property records show. In the larger transaction, the L.A.-based asset manager paid $65.3 million for a 230,147-square-foot, 15-acre distribution center at 3811 West 108th Street, located between Florida Turnpike and Interstate 75 in Hialeah. National retailer Target is the distribution center’s sole tenant after signing a 10-year lease in 2022 with two five-year extension options, according to county records. In the second sale, Ares Management paid $43.4 million for a 142,472-square-foot, 8-acre warehouse about 13 miles south at 13190 Northwest 17th Street, west of the Florida Turnpike, near Sweetwater. E-commerce parcel delivery company LaserShip has leased the entire property. BGRE, formerly called Brookfield Properties, developed both buildings, completing them between 2022 and 2023. Since opening an office in Miami Beach in 2024, Ares Management has been making inroads in South Florida’s industrial market. Last year, it purchased a 230,976-square-foot warehouse in Weston for $56 million as well as a 456,219-square-foot industrial portfolio in Broward County for $121 million. A spokesperson for Ares declined to comment, while a representative for BGRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ares Management buys two fully leased Miami warehouses from BGRE for $108.7M; Target and LaserShip sole tenants.
230k SF distribution center (Hialeah, $65.3M) and 142k SF warehouse (Sweetwater, $43.4M); completed 2022–2023.
Ares opened Miami office in 2024; industrial real estate focus indicates capital confidence, not multifamily signal.
stories.summary: Ares Management acquired two fully leased warehouses in Miami-Dade County from BGRE for a combined $108.7 million. The larger property, a 230,147-square-foot distribution center in Hialeah with a 10-year Target lease, sold for $65.3 million. A second 142,472-square-foot warehouse in Sweetwater leased to LaserShip sold for $43.4 million. Both properties were recently developed (2022–2023).
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance; Ares' Miami industrial acquisition reflects capital redeployment away from office/retail into supply-chain real estate tied to e-commerce and logistics. Indirectly, strong last-mile logistics infrastructure (Hialeah, Sweetwater locations) supports warehouse job clustering, which may drive secondary renter demand in underserved industrial submarkets; however, this is not a primary demand signal for apartment development.

stories.title: Gaia Lands Another Extension for Williamsburg Apartments’ $48M Loan
stories.excerpt: It’s déjà vu for GAIA Real Estate. The developer landed for the second straight year a one-year extension for its $48 million loan on loan with Raymond James Bank backing a multifamily property at 55 Hope Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer can first report. The extension pushed the loan maturity to August 2027, which will be five years after Gaia acquired the 1907-built and 2012-renovated apartment building previously utilized as a pencil factory. “We acquired the property at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, amid significant uncertainty in New York, and have since increased net operating income significantly through active management and a long-term approach to value creation, Danny Fishman, CEO and co-founder at Gaia Real Estate, said in a statement. “This extension demonstrates our ability to identify opportunities across market cycles and position our investments for sustained performance in Brooklyn’s multifamily market.” Fishman added that lenders were interested in refinancing the loan given that the loan is less than 50 percent loan-to-value with a “very strong” debt service coverage ratio, but he opted to go the extension route due to the current rising interest rate climate. After purchasing the 117-unit property from Hope Street Capital for $80 million in August 2022, Gaia added coworking space and refurbished the building’s rooftop while also providing tenant concessions. Hope Street Capital acquired the building for $17 million in 2010 and converted it from industrial to residential use, The Real Deal previously reported. Raymond James Bank did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: GAIA Real Estate secures second consecutive one-year extension on $48M Raymond James loan for 55 Hope Street, Williamsburg.
Maturity now August 2027 (5 years post-acquisition); 1907 building renovated 2012, NOI grown under active management.
Lender willingness to extend signals strong asset performance and Brooklyn multifamily market fundamentals despite refinance uncertainty.
stories.summary: GAIA Real Estate secured its second consecutive one-year loan extension from Raymond James Bank for a $48 million loan on 55 Hope Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, extending maturity to August 2027. The property, a 1907-built building renovated in 2012, was acquired during the COVID-19 pandemic. GAIA has increased NOI through active management and long-term value creation strategies.
stories.impact: Back-to-back extensions (rather than refinance) signal lender comfort with GAIA's execution and Williamsburg rental fundamentals, but also suggest refinance markets remain tight or rate/cap-rate environment unfavorable for full refi. For developers, Williamsburg's resilience post-COVID (acquired at peak uncertainty) and NOI growth validate niche repositioning in Brooklyn; however, extension strategy may mask underlying refinance pressure—monitor capital markets for when Brooklyn multifamily refinance activity normalizes.

stories.title: Membership Platform Patreon Renews 45K-SF Sublease at 75 Varick Street
stories.excerpt: Patreon is staying put at its offices in Manhattan’s Hudson Square. The membership and monetization platform, which allows creators to build communities and share exclusive content, has signed a sublease renewal for 44,661 square feet at Hudson Square Properties’ 75 Varick Street, according to a monthly office report from CBRE. The renewal was confirmed by Patreon. It’s unclear when the San Francisco-based company moved into the 18-story office building, also known as One Hudson Square, or who the sublandlord is. 75 Varick is a flagship property within the Hudson Square Properties portfolio, which is owned through a joint venture involving Trinity Church Wall Street and Norges Bank Investment Management. Hines was also a minority investor and operating partner in the JV, but Commercial Observer reported in July that it would no longer hold its stake in the 13-property portfolio, and that Brookfield might replace Hines by securing a 10 percent stake in the portfolio. The length of Patreon’s renewal and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from Newmark found office rents in Hudson Square averaged $91.02 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026. The brokers involved in the deal were also unclear. Spokespeople for Hudson Square Properties and CBRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Patreon shares its 75 Varick building with several other tenants, including artificial intelligence productivity software developer Notion and creative production firm RadicalMedia, which both renewed leases there in January. In fact, renewal deals appear to be popular at 75 Varick, as media company Horizon Media signed a deal there in March 2025 to keep its 360,000 square feet for another 17 years. And it’s not just 75 Varick — the entire Hudson Square neighborhood has been reaping the benefits of the city’s AI boom and increased leasing demand. bullets: Patreon renews 44,661 SF sublease at 75 Varick Street (Hudson Square), Manhattan; no term/rent disclosed.

The renewal was not detailed on term or rent. The building is part of a 13-property Hudson Square Properties portfolio owned by Trinity Church Wall Street and Norges Bank Investment Management.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact; Patreon's office renewal reflects SoHo/Hudson Square's continued appeal to tech/media tenants despite remote-work headwinds. Indirectly, sustained office occupancy in Greenwich Village/Hudson Square submarkets supports renter demand from knowledge workers; developers should continue monitoring office-to-residential conversion opportunities in this corridor, as sublease activity and tenant retention signal neighborhoods remain economically vital and attractive to younger workforces.

stories.title: Developer Ailanthus Files Plans to Build 400 Apartments at 424 Hoyt Street in Gowanus
stories.excerpt: Residential towers grow in Brooklyn. Affordable and mixed-income housing developer Ailanthus has filed a rezoning application with the New York City Department of City Planning to build a 17-story, 175-foot-tall mixed-use residential development at 424 Hoyt Street in Gowanus, Brooklyn. If approved, the building would have 400 apartment units — of which 100 to 120 would be affordable — as well as a 46,000-square-foot public school and 14,000 square feet of commercial retail space, according to the application filing. The application still has several steps to get through before approval is granted. “As noted in the Mamdani administration’s recently released report, New York City needs to create 700,000 new housing units over the next 10 years. While Gowanus contributed thousands of units in the last few years, Community Board 6, which encompasses Gowanus, was identified as one of three districts in Brooklyn with the least access to affordable homes, setting a target for thousands more units to be created there,” a spokesperson for Ailanthus told Commercial Observer. Two Trees Management acquired 424 Hoyt Street in July 2008 for $7.7 million, according to property records. Ailanthus, led by Ofer Cohen, Vivian Liao and Tucker Reed, has a ground lease at the site from Two Trees. Currently, there is a one-story automotive repair building and a vehicle storage facility on the property, which is allowed 91,800 buildable square feet. Two Trees Management declined Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Gowanus has been in the midst of a glow-up ever since its rezoning plan was initiated, not to mention a 2013 environmental cleanup plan designed to transform one of the city’s grittiest areas. The 82-block redevelopment plan passed in November of 2021. There have been several luxury and affordable housing developments delivered in Gowanus, including the Gowanus Wharf campus, 544 Carroll Street and 499 President Street. bullets: Ailanthus files rezoning for 400-unit, 17-story mixed-use at 424 Hoyt Street, Gowanus, Brooklyn; 100–120 affordable units.
Includes 46k SF public school and 14k SF retail; application in early stages; NYC targets 700k units in 10 years.

stories.summary: Ailanthus, an affordable and mixed-income housing developer, filed a rezoning application with NYC Department of City Planning for a 400-unit, 17-story mixed-use development at 424 Hoyt Street in Gowanus, Brooklyn. The project would include 100–120 affordable units, a 46,000-square-foot public school, and 14,000 square feet of commercial retail. The application is in early stages of approval.
stories.impact: Gowanus rezoning and affordability mandate signal NYC's push to densify underutilized industrial/commercial corridors with mixed-income housing near transit. For developers, City's 700k-unit goal and CB6 affordability gap create window for entitlement-ready projects combining market-rate and affordable units; however, school co-location and public review process slow timelines. Competitive tension between Ailanthus (mission-driven), market-rate builders, and affordable-only developers will intensify—monitor zoning wins and feasibility thresholds.

stories.title: HR Tech Firm Gusto Expands to 76K SF at Vornado’s Penn 1
stories.excerpt: Human resources technology company Gusto has doubled its footprint at Vornado Realty Trust’s 2.5 million-square-foot Midtown office tower Penn 1, also known as 1 Pennsylvania Plaza. The deal includes a 13-year lease expansion that added 38,000 square feet across the tower’s 47th floor. The company also opted for a five-year renewal of its 52nd-floor lease, which also spans 38,000 square feet, bringing its total footprint at the building to 76,000 square feet. The Real Deal first reported on the deal. Asking rent was $135 per square foot. CBRE’s Jeff Fisher, Sacha Zarba and Conor Krup negotiated the deal on behalf of Gusto, while Vornado’s Josh Glick, Jared Silverman and Anthony Cugini represented the landlord in-house. Penn 1, Vornado’s largest office tower in its popular Penn District, underwent a $450 million building-wide renovation in 2023, adding more than 160,000 square feet of amenities, including a restaurant and a 35,000-square-foot wellness and fitness center. The 55-story tower’s asking rents far exceed Midtown’s average office asking rent of $85.55 per square foot in August, according to CBRE data. Penn 1 tenants include high-profile firms like electronics giant Samsung, which doubled its footprint there last year, as well as technology company Dell, insurance provider United Healthcare, and financial firms Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo. Gusto, Vornado and CBRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Gusto doubles Midtown office footprint at Vornado's Penn 1 to 76k SF; 13-year expansion + 5-year renewal at $135/SF.
Added 38k SF on 47th floor, renewed 38k SF on 52nd floor; Penn 1 underwent $450M renovation in 2023.
Vornado asking rent ($135/SF) exceeds Midtown average ($85/SF); office recovery signal driven by tech/HR platforms.
stories.summary: HR technology company Gusto doubled its footprint at Vornado Realty Trust's Penn 1 (1 Pennsylvania Plaza) in Midtown Manhattan to 76,000 square feet, signing a 13-year expansion for 38,000 square feet on the 47th floor and a five-year renewal of 38,000 square feet on the 52nd floor. The asking rent was $135 per square foot, well above Midtown's average of $85 per square foot. Penn 1 underwent a $450 million renovation in 2023.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily relevance; Gusto's expansion reflects tech/SaaS sector's sustained Midtown office demand despite hybrid-work trends and overall NYC office softness. Indirectly, Penn 1's $450M upgrade and ability to command $135/SF (60% premium to Midtown average) signal landlord confidence and that trophy office assets with world-class amenities retain pricing power, supporting Midtown's overall economic vitality and renter demand among white-collar workers—a secondary demand factor for luxury multifamily in Midtown East/West.
